A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MATRIX/MATRIX-Gen research. Their text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original fine-tuning experiments, domain-specific evaluations, communication and scaling ablations, and additional experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains original experimental results and adds broader benchmark evaluations, reasoning experiments, realism comparisons, anonymization measurements, and contamination analyses.

M1.justification: The simulator, communication mechanism, and standard SFT/DPO pipeline remain substantively unchanged. v2 adds a reasoning-data branch using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B responses, filtering excessively long reasoning traces and balancing their length distribution (Section 4.2; Appendix C.3). The renamed homophily-guided communication is the existing structured mechanism.

E1.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluated task coverage through MMLU, IFEval, GSM8K, MATH, MATH-500, AIME, and GPQA Diamond, adding explicit knowledge, constrained instruction-following, mathematics, and scientific reasoning evaluations. The original general instruction-following, coding, dialogue, and safety coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds Tulu 3 to the SFT and DPO comparisons and introduces six reasoning comparators, including Camel MATH, PersonaHub-Math, Numina MATH, and Tulu 3 Math/Code (Tables 1–3). Conversely, Magpie and Evol Instruct disappear from the dedicated coding and safety comparisons when v1 Tables 6–7 become v2 Figure 5.

E3.justification: The Qwen2-7B evaluation in v1 Appendix A.2 is replaced by Qwen-2.5-7B experiments. New reasoning comparisons use a common DeepSeek response generator, while new analyses introduce realism classification, entity recognition, and embedding-distance procedures. The standard 10K-sample, two-epoch training budget and listed fine-tuning hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds realistic-versus-non-realistic instruction training, direct communication-related diversity/realism measurements, anonymization audits, contamination checks, and reasoning-length analyses. It removes v1 Appendix A.1's simple-versus-complex SFT/DPO ablation. Existing agent/scenario scaling and instruction quality/difficulty analyses are retained, with some relocated.

E5.justification: SD columns disappear from the matched SFT, DPO, and communication comparisons formerly presented in v1 Tables 2, 3, and 8. SD reporting survives in v2 Table 7 and appears in its motivation experiment, Table 5. Neither version specifies a repeated-run or seed protocol.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark and diagnostic results; its new reasoning comparison reports a 50.72 average for MATRIX-Gen-Reason versus 46.42 for Tulu 3 Code. The headline Llama results remain 24.20 AlpacaEval LC, 31.30 WR, and 22.7 Arena-Hard WR. Earlier data-type ablation results and dialogue ability sub-scores are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly defines the relative property score as Rp = S_baseline/S_ours for the diversity and realism comparisons. This is a limited mathematical-definition addition; neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The multi-agent scenario-generation contribution, realism/controllability claims, and 20K-versus-10M headline remain. v2 modestly broadens the claimed capability: its introduction explicitly includes mathematical performance, and the framework now includes reasoning-data synthesis alongside the previously described dataset types.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning reasoning-length imbalance, privacy preservation through simulated interactions, and the absence of detected contamination (Appendices B.1 and C.2–C.3). Section 7 explicitly acknowledges persistent inference costs. The earlier interpretation favoring simple SFT followed by complex DPO data loses its dedicated analysis.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents X profile collection using 175 Alpaca instructions, 500 search tags, top-three-user retrieval, deduplication, and tweet processing. It also supplies anonymization and realism prompts and tools for the added analyses. These substantially expand documentation of the existing pipeline, although the project link in v1's abstract is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations for Star-Agents, OASIS, Tulu 3, DeepSeek-R1, and reasoning datasets and benchmarks. The central positioning against seed/template-based synthesis and non-interacting persona approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and communication explanation are substantially rewritten, terminology changes to homophily-guided communication, and the experimental narrative is reorganized. Quality/difficulty discussion moves into Appendix C, instruction examples become Appendix D, and a separate limitations section replaces the earlier future-work ending.

P2.justification: The paper switches from a single-column to a two-column main layout. Domain tables become the consolidated Figure 5, the communication table becomes an expanded Figure 7, and new benchmark tables and diagnostic plots appear. Existing diagrams and histograms are also relocated, including v1 Figure 2 becoming v2 Figure 11.

improvement.justification: Broader objective evaluations, the realism experiment, and explicit profile-collection and anonymization procedures make v2's claims more assessable. The net gain is limited by removal of the SFT/DPO data-type ablation and some uncertainty reporting, plus overstrong interpretations: Table 1 does not show uniform superiority, and Table 22 includes a closest MBPP match requiring the same task despite the broad no-contamination conclusion. Evidence and transparency improve, but important validation weaknesses remain.
